MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  NOVEMBER 19, 2018

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
  called to order at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos
  Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California by CHAIR ROMANELLI.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  CHAIR ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Pope, Romanelli, Retz, Wroan, Ciarolla,

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Persichina

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OCTOBER 15, 2018

  B.  JOINT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL – PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF OCTOBER 30, 2018

  VICE CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CIOROLLA to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  OCTOBER 15, 2018 AND THE JOINT ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL/PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF OCTOBER 30, 2018.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA
  None

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR
  None

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  “BUTCHER PARK” REVISED CONCEPTUAL DESIGN

  Community Services Director Clark provided a summary of the staff report and stated that
  at the last meeting there was discussion which included further cost saving measures.
  Staff provided a list of items that the City could provide at no cost including, wood chips
  (including maintenance crew spreading wood chips), boulders, soil materials, the
  installation of the drip irrigation system, and finish grading work as needed. The project
  cost estimate is $97,384 along with a 10% contingency in the amount of $7,915.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and
  Activities Commission makes a recommendation to City Council to approve the “Butcher
  Park” conceptual plan and cost estimate and direct BMLA to prepare the plans and
  specifications for the bidding of this park development project.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ asked if the mobilization cost of $9K is “not to exceed”. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that it is an estimate for the selected firm to bring in
  containers and equipment.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ asked if the line item for hardscape - play surface engineered wood
  fiber is different from the wood chips that the city can provide. Community Services

Meeting Minutes  1
Park and Activities Commission
November 19, 2018
   Director Clark stated that the engineered wood fiber is different and is the material that is
  required to go around the play equipment for ADA compliance.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI stated that there were quite a few items that were cut from the project
  which the city could provide and asked what was added back to the project. Community
  Services Director stated that there was nothing added to the project and stated that the
  slide which was removed is something that could be added in the future.

  A discussion ensued regarding the items that the city could provide.

  Ed Mohr, Secretary, Montecillo Homeowners Association, asked if the parking along Palos
  Verdes Drive East adjacent to the park and there are “No Parking” signs, however, the
  area is being used for parking. Community Services Director Clark stated that he spoke
  with the City’s Traffic Engineer who confirmed that the two signs may be removed and
  create a couple of parking spaces.

  Mr. Mohr asked about access to the park aside from Palos Verdes Drive North and stated
  that there is a horse trail which he believes goes behind the homes on Casaba. There
  could also be access from a short trail from the end of Casaba over the berm. Community
  Services Director stated that there is a trail that leads to the new homes and added that
  staff will look into this further.

  In response to a question by VICE CHAIR RETZ, Mr. Mohr stated that the he can put the
  benches and trail improvements on the “hot list” for scout projects.

  Graham Sutherland, Montecillo Neighborhood Resident, questioned the purpose of the
  park since it does not seem kid-friendly and stated that he would have liked to see more
  green open space. VICE CHAIR RETZ stated that the park is very small and there is not
  large green grass area but there are things like swing and features for children to climb.
  Mr. Sutherland asked if the landscaping is necessary and shift the focus more on the play
  equipment and seating.

  Ryan McCormick, asked about the name for the park and stated that he would resend a
  list of names that he suggested. He also stated that handicap parking should be made
  available. Mr. McCormick suggested a safety fence with a gate with a latch. VICE CHAIR
  RETZ stated that there will be barriers in the form of boulders. Mr. McCormick also
  suggested chicken wire added to the 3-rail fence. In addition, he would like to circular
  swing be considered as well as a more cost effective slide added to the design.

  Sally Kensey, 22 Pony Lane, expressed concern with shade in the play areas and stated
  that only the sycamore trees are shade trees and the others are not. Ms. Kensey
  suggested that the boulders be installed in a way that the kids could enjoy and provided
  the suggestion of having tunnels.

  Further discussion ensued regarding the public’s comments being incorporated into the
  design and whether or not to move forward with staff’s recommendation.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  ONE MORE ITERATION WITH BMLA TO INCLUDE THE COST OF A CIRCULAR
  SWING, SLIDE, LARGER SHADE TREES, SAFETY FENCING AND GATES.
  ALSO CONSIDER, LESS LANDSCAPE TO ALLOW FOR GROWTH IN THE
  FUTURE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  B.  NATURE CENTER REPLACEMENT STUDY CONSULTANT

  Community Services Director Clark stated that VICE CHAIR RETZ, Executive Director,
  PVPLC, Andrea Vona, and staff members, Alexa Davis, David Wahba, and he met with
  four firms to prepare the Nature Center replacement study. The firm Roesling Nakamura
  Terada Architects in conjunction with Spurlock Landscape Architects came in on top.
  Community Services Director Clark stated that he contacted references and the public
  agencies they have done projects for were highly satisfied with the firms.

Meeting Minutes  2
Park and Activities Commission
November 19, 2018
   Community Services Director Clark stated that the interview panel recommends that the
  Park and Activities Commission make a recommendation to City Council to enter into an
  agreement with Roesling Nakamura Terada Architects in conjunction with Spurlock
  Landscape Architects to complete a Nature Center Replacement Study for the George F.
  Canyon Nature Center.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ provided further details on the interview and outcome to select the
  firm for this project.

  The Park and Activities Commission held a brief discussion on the projected budget for
  the actual construction cost and other possible funding sources.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to,

  Approve the interview panel’s recommendation to make a recommendation  to
  the City Council to enter into an agreement with Roesling Nakamura Terada
  Architects in conjunction with Spurlock Landscape Architects to complete a
  Nature Center Replacement Study for the George F. Canyon Nature
  Center.

  AYES:  Pope, Romanelli, Retz, Wroan, Ciarolla
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Persichina
  ABSTAIN:

  C.  CITY HALL COUNCIL CHAMBER PATIO RE-DESIGN

  Community Services Director Clark stated that two mature trees were removed from the
  patio area outside of the City Hall Council Chamber due to roots growing under the
  building. City Council has asked that a subcommittee be assigned to work with staff and
  Bennett Landscaping to determine the design of the patio.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and
  Activities Commission assign a subcommittee to assist staff and Bennett Landscape in
  the redesign of the City Hall Council Chamber patio re-design.

  Commissioner Ciarolla volunteered to be on the subcommittee.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR RETZ to,

  APPROVE STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION TO ASSIGN A SUBCOMMITTEE TO
  ASSIST STAFF AND BENNETT LANDSCAPE IN THE REDESIGN OF THE CITY
  HALL COUNCIL CHAMBER PATIO RE-DESIGN.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  D.  COMMITTEE AND SUBCOMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

  Commissioner Pope stated that she would be happy to move to another subcommittee
  and expressed interest in serving on the Tennis Tournament and Parade Subcommittees.

  Commissioner Ciarolla expressed interest in being on the Equestrian Committee and the
  Hills Are Alive subcommittee.

  The Park and Activities Commission agreed to table this item to the next Park and
  Activities Committee meeting.

  E.  PARK REGULATIONS AND PERMIT FEES (Verbal Report)

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there are no regulations to have larger
  tents installed at Ernie Howlett Park. He also stated that there are no established fees for
  festivals.
  A brief discussion ensued on this item.

Meeting Minutes  3
Park and Activities Commission
November 19, 2018
   CHAIR ROMANELLI expressed his interest on being on a subcommittee to work on park
  regulations and permit fees. Community Services Director Clark stated that he will contact
  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA since he may also have interest on being on this
  committee.

  F.  PROPOSED PARKWAY PLANTINGS

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the City Council would like to add
  bougainvillea plants to add more color to the parkways. The proposed cost would be
  approximately $1,400 and would come from the city’s general fund.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and
  Activities Commission make a recommendation to City Council to approve the planting of
  Bougainvillea Vines in selected locations along Palos Verdes Drive North.

  A brief discussion ensued on toxicity to horses and any additional maintenance costs and
  determined that neither is an issue.

  VICE CHAIR RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  APPROVE STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION TO MAKE A RECOMMENDATION
  TO CITY COUNCIL TO APPROVE THE PLANTING OF BOUGAINVILLEA VINES
  IN SELECTED LOCATIONS ALONG PALOS VERDES DRIVE NORTH.

  AYES:  Pope, Romanelli, Retz, Wroan, Ciarolla
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Persichina
  ABSTAIN:

  8.  COMMISSION ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the company that was supposed to install new
  fencing. Community Services Director Clark stated that staff is awaiting direction from the
  City Attorney on how to proceed.

  CHAIR ROMANELLI provided an update on the Youth Sports Subcommittee meeting and
  stated that they met with the leadership of Silver Spur Little League last week. The
  enrollment period opened November 1st and they have half as many as last year in the
  first month. There was also discussion on the responsibilities of Silver Spur Little League
  versus the City and confirmed that the little league will be taking care of the infields at
  Ernie Howlett Park and Highridge Park and city staff/maintenance will take care of the
  outfields. Opening day will be the first Saturday in March. A league representative will
  contact staff regarding who they would like to be present for opening day. They requested
  that the maintenance department take a look at the electrical box and hose bib that may
  need repair at Ernie Howlett Park. He also mentioned that there have been times when
  practices have gone on after hours and staff will work on exact closing times and
  communicate that to the league.

  9.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  DECEMBER 17, 2018 COMMISSION MEETING QUORUM

  It was determined that there will be a quorum for the December 17, 2018 Park and
  Activities Commission meeting.

  B.  HARBOR SIGHT DRIVE RESIDENT ENCROACHMENT UPDATE

  Community Services Director Clark stated that there is a Phase 1 and Phase 2 of the John
  and Lynn Taber Grove pocket park project. Phase 2 was dependent on a survey and it
  clearly shows several encroachments. A copy of the certified survey and a letter was sent
  to the property owners to set-up a meeting with city staff.

Meeting Minutes  4
Park and Activities Commission
November 19, 2018
   In response to a question by CHAIR ROMANELLI, the next step is for the City Council to
  either grant or deny encroachment permits.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF OCTOBER 23, 2018

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF NOVEMBER 13, 2018

  C.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 5, 2018

  VICE CHAIR RETZ moved to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 10-A TO 10-C

  There being no objection, CHAIR ROMANELLI so ordered.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  DEVELOP PUBLIC LANDSCAPING SUGGESTIONS FOR CITY OF PALOS VERDES
  ESTATES

  COMMISSIONER WROAN stated that the City of Palos Verdes Estates has announced
  in their newsletter that they have a program to address the landscaping. No further
  discussion is necessary.

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ROMANELLI adjourned the meeting at 8:30 p.m. to the next Park and Activities
  Commission meeting on Monday, December 17, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council
  Chamber at City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Administrative Assistant  City Clerk

Meeting Minutes  5
Park and Activities Commission
November 19, 2018
